items.title: Snakes, swings and stuck rings: Fire Dept's strangest rescues
items.summary: While the Fire and Rescue Department is best known for fighting fires and responding to road accidents, it is increasingly called upon to handle unusual rescue operations that require precision, patience and compassion. Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said it handled 72,977 special rescue operations nationwide last year, a 10.1 per cent increase from 66,299 cases in 2024. "It also reflects the expanding scope of the department's responsibilities, which now covers a wide range of incidents requiring specialised rescue expertise."

items.title: Lala, now a hurricane, dumps heavy rain on Hawaii
items.summary: HONOLULU: Hurricane Lala on Saturday lashed Hawaii's Big Island with heavy rain and strong winds, as forecasters warned of potentially dangerous flooding across the US Pacific island state. Lala strengthened into a Category 1 hurricane at around 9am local time (1900 GMT), packing winds of up to 75 miles per hour (120 kilometres per hour). A hurricane warning was in effect for Hawaii County, which covers the Big Island, and a tropical storm warning was in place for the state's seven other major islands: Maui, Molokai, Kahoolawe, Lanai, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau.

items.title: Iran fires back at Trump's threat to declare Hormuz a US territory
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran on Saturday fired back at US President Donald Trump's claim that he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz part of US territory, saying the crucial energy waterway it has blockaded "will remain Iranian." "The Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian," Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on X. "This strait will only be closed and opened under Iran's command."

items.title: Opposition walkouts may win headlines but lose the debate
items.summary: Several opposition MPs walked out after their bid to postpone the sitting until Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim could attend was rejected. Opposition chief whip Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the Tabung Haji issue was significant enough to warrant the prime minister's presence, particularly as Anwar had previously addressed it. When the sitting proceeded with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and other ministers present, several opposition MPs left the chamber.

items.title: Parliamentary walkouts: When protest becomes the story
items.summary: This was evident during the Dewan Rakyat sitting, when most opposition members of parliament left over Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's absence, while others, including Bersatu MPs, stayed to participate in the debate. Rayer criticised the walkout, saying opposition MPs should have remained to scrutinise the RCI findings. The latest walkout, however, was defended by Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal, who said the opposition was seeking a more thorough debate involving Anwar.

items.title: From rice to remedy: Penang maker’s time‑honoured 40‑day method keeps traditional ‘bedak sejuk’ craft alive
items.summary: Over the years, however, bedak sejuk gradually fell out of favour, often regarded as an old-fashioned product used mainly by older generations. But in recent years, traditional bedak sejuk has begun to regain popularity, helped by greater public interest in heritage products, according to maker Yeoh Siong Huat. Yeoh said his parents had previously operated a small-scale business rearing pigs while also producing belacan and bedak sejuk for sale.

items.title: Fire dept calls for systematic measures to prevent fallen tree incidents nationwide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Incidents of fallen trees in Malaysia can no longer be considered isolated incidents that only occur during the rainy season; instead, they require a preventive approach that is more systematic through regular safety audits, inter-agency data sharing and consistent maintenance. Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) statistics show that 26,001 cases of fallen trees were recorded nationwide from 2021 to June, last year, resulting in 50 fatalities and 243 injuries. Its director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said that emergency calls related to fallen trees remain consistently high, ranging between 4,400 and 5,200 cases per year, while for the first half of 2026 alone, 1,912 cases were recorded.

items.title: Raja Muda of Selangor officiates opening of 2026 Sukma
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The opening ceremony of the 22nd Malaysia Games (Sukma) and Para Sukma 2026 was held at Dataran Kemerdekaan Shah Alam here last night. The ceremony was officiated by the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah. Selangor last hosted the Games in 1998.

items.title: Bersama announces 15 candidates for Melaka election
items.summary: MELAKA: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) last night announced its 15 candidates for the Melaka election. The announcement was made by the party's co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli at a ceremony in Batu Berendam here. The Bersama candidates for the Melaka election are as follows: N.01 Kuala Linggi - Datuk Ruzsyahriman Jenal N.06 Rembia - Mohamed Aman Akil Abdul Talib N.07 Gadek - B. Laveen N.08 Machap Jaya - Prasanth Kumar Brakasam N.11 Sungai Udang - Mohd Ridzuan Abdul Rahman N.13 Paya Rumput - Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar N.14 Kelebang - Young Jie Yu N.15 Pengkalan Batu - Goh Han Koon N.16 Ayer Keroh - Muhammad Muhaimin Lau Abdullah N.17 Bukit Katil - Dr Aliza Che Amran N.19 Kesidang - Dr Bryan Kek Kit Hun N.20 Kota Laksamana - Ethan Lim Zhi Hao N.23 Telok Mas - Muhammad Hazwan Mustafa N.24 Bemban - Dr Muhammad Solehin Saleh N.26 Serkam - Muhamad Saffie Md Yasan © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: University student loses RM29,000 in phone scam
items.summary: IPOH: A 22-year-old university student lost RM29,000 after falling victim to a phone scam involving callers posing as a courier company representative and a law enforcement officer. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the victim received a call on July 31 from a caller posing as a delivery company representative, who claimed that a parcel containing prohibited items had been sent in his name. Alwi said the victim was told the cash and jewellery would be returned once the alleged investigation was completed.

items.title: Two drivers held for blocking traffic to let supercar convoy pass
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police have detained two car drivers believed to have acted as "marshals" by obstructing traffic to allow a luxury car convoy to pass at Bulatan Lebuh Kota Iskandar here. Iskandar Puteri deputy police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said both men were detained yesterday by the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division. "Acting on a public complaint, the Iskandar Puteri District Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division conducted an operation to trace the individuals involved.

items.title: Penang remains under control after North Sumatra quake
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The situation in Penang remains under control after tremors from a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in North Sumatra, Indonesia , were felt across the state this evening. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow urged the public to remain calm as authorities continued monitoring the situation. Chow said the state government had received a report from the Penang Fire and Rescue Department's Operations Control Centre on the tremors following the earthquake in Indonesia.

items.title: At least 47 dead in eastern Indonesia after magnitude 7.7 quake
items.summary: JAKARTA: At least 47 people were killed after a magnitude 7.7 earthquake and dozens of aftershocks struck off eastern Indonesia on Saturday, the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) said in its latest statement. Rescue teams have yet to reach Nagekeo, the region closest to the epicentre, after landslides blocked roads and disrupted communications, officials said. "The quake was massive, the shock was so strong," said Nona, a 51-year-old resident of Talibura, a village in East Nusa Tenggara.

items.title: No damage, casualties after earthquake tremors felt at nine Penang premises
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: No damage or casualties were reported after tremors from a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in North Sumatra were felt at nine premises across Penang tonight. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said checks carried out at all nine locations found no incidents or hazards. "A total of 36 personnel, supported by four fire rescue tenders, two light fire rescue tenders and three Emergency Medical Rescue Services vehicles, were involved in the operation," he added.

items.title: NST Leader: Is 'cash for stray dogs' the right approach?
items.summary: "CASH for stray dogs" should not become a false choice between protecting public safety and protecting animal welfare. Granted, local councils have a duty to address dangerous stray animals, but the method adopted must command public confidence, minimise unintended consequences and uphold professional standards. Although there aren't any official figures about the number of stray dogs in Negri Sembilan, the "cash for stray dogs" plan sure reads like an act of desperation.

items.title: US says more oil is leaving Hormuz, but the numbers don't add up
items.summary: He further said that adding in an "additional 5-7 million bpd leaving the region via newly upgraded pipelines and export facilities, total oil flows are currently averaging approximately 15 million bpd". Wright didn't specify the exact time period for his seven-day average, but data from commodity analysts Kpler shows crude exports via Hormuz for the week beginning July 27 at 2.77 million bpd. Kpler data shows crude shipments of 9.53 million bpd in the week beginning Aug 3, and a four-week average of 12.26 million bpd.

items.title: Stray dogs spark safety fears in Kajang village
items.summary: KAJANG: Residents of Kampung Sungai Sekamat are concerned over the growing number of stray dogs roaming the area, with some fearing for the safety of children and students. According to a report by Buletin TV3, residents said nearly 30 stray dogs were roaming the neighbourhood, particularly from evening into the night, with the problem persisting for almost 5 years. The incident heightened concerns among residents over the risks posed by dogs roaming the roads.

items.title: Woman who died after headscarf entangled in floodgate roller was on duty
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Md Yusof Ahmad said the 55-year-old woman worked as a DID floodgate operator in Sabak Bernam. "However, an accident occurred, resulting in the woman's death," he said when contacted. Md Yusof said police received a report on the incident about 4pm.

items.title: S. Korea's blind fortune-tellers could not see AI coming
items.summary: CLIENTS have drifted away from Song Oh-soon's fortune-telling village on the edge of Seoul, preferring online artificial intelligence-powered divination to the centuries-old prophesying tradition still practiced there. "There were people who came here wanting to die," Song said in northern Seoul's Mia village. Today, silence is often Song's only visitor.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin graces National Month programme in Perak
items.summary: IPOH: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today graced a programme aimed at instilling loyalty to the King and country in conjunction with National Month 2026. Zulkafli said the programme also supported Perak's education vision of producing students who were not only academically excellent but also possessed good character, critical thinking skills and a strong patriotic spirit. Zulkafli said 2028 would mark a historic milestone for Perak with the celebration of the 500th anniversary of the Perak Sultanate.

items.title: Police probe FB account over alleged sedition, insults against royal institution
items.summary: CHUKAI: Police are investigating the owner of the Facebook account 'Ahmad Mu'min' over a post suspected of containing elements of sedition and insulting the royal institution, the Malaysian government and the police. Kemaman district police chief Superintendent Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 was launched after a report was lodged by a 29-year-old man at 11.14am today. "The police will investigate the identity of the account owner and subsequently conduct an investigation in accordance with legal procedures," he said in a statement today.

items.title: 'We thought we were dizzy,' says Penang resident as tremors also felt in Perak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck northern Sumatra, Indonesia, at 6.54pm today, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said. In Penang, state Fire and Rescue Department director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said the departmen t received nine emergency calls regarding the tremors about 6.55pm. He said the calls involved four areas in two districts on the island, as well as several areas in Seberang Perai.

items.title: Tiny Tun Ms and Siti Hasmahs steal the spotlight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Young lookalikes of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, charmed the crowd at a costume contest held to mark his 101st birthday. "It was a Tun Dr Mahathir and Tun Siti Hasmah lookalike contest, where participants mimicked the duo's signature styles," he told the New Straits Times. Alif said 15 children took part, with two boys dressed as Mahathir and 13 girls as Siti Hasmah.

items.title: Audit findings crucial to strengthening public sector accountability, says AG
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Audit Department is carrying out its mandate as the country's audit institution independently, professionally and with integrity to strengthen accountability, transparency and governance in the public sector, says Auditor General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi. She said audit findings were compiled in the Auditor General's Report (LKAN), an important instrument in the country's checks-and-balances mechanism. Wan Suraya said the Auditor General's role in providing opinions on financial statements and making audit recommendations was not merely to fulfil reporting requirements to Parliament, but more importantly, to encourage effective corrective action and improvements in public sector management.

items.title: Sarawak wants transboundary haze issue tackled at Asean level
items.summary: KUCHING: The transboundary haze issue in Sarawak should continue to be discussed at the Asean level through the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee on Transboundary Haze Pollution to find effective solutions to minimise its impact. Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry, which represents Malaysia on the committee, would put forward proposals to address the issue. Yesterday, Uggah said cloud seeding was being considered to address prolonged hot and dry weather conditions, which could affect water sources and worsen haze conditions in several areas.

items.title: Sabah teacher uses Jawi to bridge cultural and religious differences in Beluran
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — For Lorenica Frenila Masundim, teaching Jawi script at a school in Sabah’s interior is more than a lesson in writing, it is a way of bringing students and the wider community closer while fostering understanding across racial, religious and cultural differences. Lorenica said she found great fulfilment in seeing non-Muslim students who were once unfamiliar with Jawi gradually learn to read and understand their function as part of the Malay writing system. Lorenica was first introduced to the Jawi script in 2009 when she took the Basic Introduction to Jawi Writing course for one semester at the Institute of Teacher Education, Gaya Campus in Kota Kinabalu.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Saturday, Aug 15, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1511844]] [[nid:1511843]] [[nid:1511842]] [[nid:1511841]] [[nid:1511840]] [[nid:1511839]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Sign language opens doors to Islamic learning for Kelantan deaf community
items.summary: KOTA BARU: For members of the Kelantan Deaf Association, hearing impairment is no barrier to learning the basics of Islam, with about 100 members attending Fardu Ain classes twice a month to deepen their understanding of religious teachings. The classes use a simple but effective approach, with religious officers from the Kelantan Islamic Religious Affairs Department delivering lessons through normal speech while a sign language interpreter translates the teachings for participants. "The lessons are conducted manually, with the interpreter translating what the religious officer explains into sign language," she said.

items.title: MCMC boosts UTeM's digital connectivity, benefiting more than 12,000 students
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: More than 12,000 students at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) are benefiting from upgraded digital infrastructure, including 410 Wi-Fi access points (APs) and a new 4G communications tower at the university. The Universal Service Provision (USP) project, implemented by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), is expected to strengthen connectivity across the campus, particularly to support learning, teaching and training under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system. "It will help strengthen communications coverage while improving the quality and user experience of digital services among the campus community," MCMC said in a statement today.

items.title: [UPDATED] North Sumatra quake sends tremors across several parts of Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Tremors from a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in North Sumatra, Indonesia, were felt in several parts of Penang this evening, with five reports received by authorities. The Fire and Rescue Department confirmed receiving five reports of tremors, four from Penang island and one from the mainland. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis, when contacted, confirmed that five reports had been received so far.

items.title: Sabah leaders’ presence at PKR congress reflects strong ties, cooperation, says Mustapha
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman, and other leaders’ attendance at the 2026 PKR National Congress today reflects the strong ties and spirit of cooperation between Sabah and federal governments. Sabah PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the cooperation extended beyond politics, encompassing all aspects. Among the GRS leaders present were Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Sabah Rural Development Minister Datuk Rubin Balang and Sabah Youth, Sports Development and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan.

items.title: Auditor-general: Audit reports key to strengthening accountability, transparency and governance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The National Audit Department (JAN) is carrying out its mandate as the country’s audit institution independently, professionally and with integrity in strengthening accountability, transparency and governance in the public sector, says Auditor General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi. She said audit findings were translated into the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN), which is one of the important instruments in the country’s checks-and-balances mechanism. She said the Auditor General’s firmness in providing opinions on Financial Statements and making audit recommendations was not merely to fulfil reporting requirements to Parliament, but more importantly, to encourage effective corrective action and improvements in public sector management.

items.title: Several Sepang roads to close for Sukma cycling event
items.summary: "The traffic control duties will be divided into four zones, namely Zone A, covering Jalan Pantai Sepang Putra to the Tumbuk border; Zone B, Jalan Dengkil-Jenderam Hulu; Zone C, Jalan Jenderam-Salak; and Zone D, Jalan Salak Sepang-Sungai Pelek. Meanwhile, the Aug 18 road closures will involve 18 locations, including Persiaran Pantai Sepang Putra, Jalan Kampung Bagan Lalang, Jalan Bukit Bangkong-Tanjung Rhu, Jalan Tumbuk Sempadan, Jalan Banting-Semenyih (Dengkil-bound) and the Pekan Dengkil traffic lights. Also affected are the Simpang Empat Dengkil traffic lights (Jenderam-bound), Jalan Jenderam Hilir, Jalan Jenderam-Salak, Simpang Taman Mawar-BBST, Jalan Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi, Jalan Salak Tinggi (Medan 88), Jalan Kompleks Kerajaan Daerah Sepang and Jalan Pekan Salak-Lembah Paya.

items.title: On-demand car sharing platform, Socar is shutting down in Malaysia after 8 years of operations.
items.summary: Effective today, the Socar app will no longer accept Wallet top-ups and new monthly pass subscriptions. However, take note that only Socar will cease operations as its peer-to-peer service, Trevo, is still available in Malaysia. Unlike Socar which essentially works like an on-demand car rental service, Trevo is essentially an “Airbnb” of sorts for car sharing.

items.title: KDM rep attends GRS assemblymen's programme amid support withdrawal
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) sole elected representative Datuk Rusdin Rimad attended a programme with other Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) assemblymen here this morning, amid his party's announcement that it was withdrawing its support for the coalition. GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said he had contacted the Paginatan assemblyman following KDM acting president Priscella Peter's announcement that the party was withdrawing its support for GRS. Armizan, who is also Papar member of parliament, said KDM was not a component party of GRS.

items.title: Flores earthquake: 16 Malaysian tourists safe, says embassy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A group of 16 Malaysian tourists who were in areas affected by a magnitude 7.7 earthquake on Flores Island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, were confirmed safe and in good health. In a media advisory on Saturday, the Foreign Ministry said the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta had established contact with the group following the earthquake, which struck northeast of Mbay in Nagekeo Regency at 4.58am local time. The ministry said the embassy was actively coordinating with the relevant local authorities to ascertain the safety and well-being of Malaysians in the affected areas.

items.title: Fahmi: PKR to strengthen communication strategy to better convey govt messages
items.summary: PKR Information Chief, who is also Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, said the move followed several proposals raised by delegates at the ongoing PKR National Congress 2026 at the Melaka International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh. “This is important (to strengthen information dissemination and communication). Fahmi said several views and planned changes related to information dissemination and communication proposals would be presented during the winding-up session tomorrow.

items.title: PKR Selangor delegate calls for party to use own logo in Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — A Selangor PKR delegate today proposed that the party return to using its own logo in future elections, starting with the upcoming Melaka state election. Ahmad Danish Hairudin, who is also PKR national Youth information chief, said it was timely for the party to campaign under its own logo in the state polls. PKR has used its iconic blue-and-white logo in several elections.

items.title: Myanmar refugee, two young sons die in Bagan Serai house fire
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 15 — Three Myanmar refugees comprising a man and his two sons, died while his wife was injured in a house fire in Taman Serai Maju, Bagan Serai, early this morning. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the deceased victims were identified as Mohd Yunus Nor Ali, 27, Muhammad Woheed Mohd Yunus, 6, and Mohamad Aheed Mohd Yunus, 3, while the victim’s wife, Saniya Jahan Juma Abul Kasim, 24, who is also a Myanmar refugee, suffered burns on her hands and feet. Sayani said that upon arriving at the location, his team immediately conducted a search and rescue operation using the RECEO concept before three victims were found in the first room that was on fire.

items.title: Subang airport runway reopens after helicopter explosion, eight flights diverted
items.summary: SUBANG, Aug 15 — The runway at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here has been reopened after being temporarily closed following a helicopter exploding and catching fire during an engine run-up test earlier this afternoon. Malaysian Civil Aviation Authority (CAAM) chief executive officer Capt Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the incident occurred at Taxiway Victor, leading to a temporary suspension of flights. Norazman said during the runway closure, eight inbound flights were diverted to other airports, while three departing flights had to be delayed.

items.title: Not our facility, not our customer: Aviation company distances itself from Subang helicopter fire
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 15 — An aviation maintenance company today denied any connection to the Kamov Ka-32 helicopter that caught fire at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here, saying the aircraft was not its customer and the incident did not occur at its facility. The clarification by KarbonMRO came after the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department said the helicopter caught fire during an engine test following maintenance work at the airport, with four people escaping, one who was injured by debris. The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the incident occurred at Taxiway Victor, temporarily disrupting airport operations before the runway reopened at 2.57pm.

items.title: No Malaysians reported affected by earthquake in Indonesia’s Flores, says embassy
items.summary: JAKARTA, Aug 15 — No Malaysians have been reported affected by the magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck Flores in Indonesia’s East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) province early today. The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta said it had contacted Malaysians in NTT who were registered with the embassy, as well as Malaysian tourists who had informed the embassy of their whereabouts in the region. Malaysians affected by the earthquake and requiring consular assistance can contact the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta via +62 813 8081 3036 or email mwjakarta@kln.gov.my.

items.title: ‘Beginning, not the end’: Abim calls for broader higher education reform after AUKU repeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) 1971 will create new opportunities to reform the country’s higher education framework, said the Muslim Youth Movement of Malaysia (Abim). Welcoming the move to repeal the Act, Abim president Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Samsudin called on the government to formulate a comprehensive post-AUKU legal framework covering the country’s entire higher education ecosystem. He said the focus should now be on building a new higher education ecosystem that strikes a balance between student freedom and strong institutional governance.

items.title: As PKR grapples with departures, Anwar makes fresh appeal for estranged old friends to return
items.summary: AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today appealed to former PKR leaders and members who have drifted away from the party to return, while apologising to those who may have felt sidelined. His call comes as PKR faces a series of internal tensions and recent departures, including former Subang MP Wong Chen who quit the party earlier this week, while former leaders Chua Tian Chang and Dr Xavier Jayakumar were seen at the party’s national congress here today. “ .. please return,” Anwar was quoted by news portal Malaysiakini as saying in his policy speech at the PKR National Congress 2026 at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.

items.title: Motac cracks down on unlicensed tourism operators in KL, issues 15 notices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) issued 15 inspection notices for various offences under the Tourism Industry Act 1992 (Act 482) during a two-day enforcement operation that began on Wednesday around Kuala Lumpur. In a statement today, Motac said nine of the notices were issued under Subsection 5(2) for operating a tourism business without a valid licence. “Three tourist locations, nine business premises and three individuals were inspected over the course of the operation.

items.title: Federal govt aims to cut Terengganu poor households to 20,000 by year-end
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 15 — The federal government aims to reduce the number of poor households in Terengganu to 20,000 by this December. Deputy director-general of the Strategic Development, Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU), under the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM), Datuk Norashiken Ishak, said as of August 13, the number of poor households in Terengganu was recorded at 24,100 households, compared to 26,800 households in early July. She also said the total includes 161 new construction projects, 146 house renovation projects, and three new stilt house construction projects.

items.title: Sabah hospital sexual harassment case: MOH moves director out, complainant under treatment, PSD to decide next step
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Health Ministry has completed its internal investigation into an alleged sexual harassment case involving a Sabah hospital director and transferred the officer to a medical post at the Sabah Health Department. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry had also submitted its report to the Public Service Department (PSD), which has jurisdiction over further action based on the officer’s grade, The New Straits Times reported. “Administratively, the ministry has completed the internal investigation.

items.title: Five PKR figures honoured with posthumous awards
items.summary: Four received the Bill Kayong Award, while the fifth was awarded the Dr Syed Husin Ali Pejuang Rakyat Award, introduced for the first time in recognition of the late Syed Husin’s contributions as a PKR founder and advocate of social justice. The Bill Kayong Award was presented to the late Sapiah Zaini, former Miri Women’s chief; the late Hasbul Syafiqi Hasbullah, Keadilan Penang working secretary; and party activists, the late Syafiq Ali Abdullah@Abang Mani, and the late Muhammad Shahhanaz Nazarudin. The award, named after the late Sarawak activist Bill Kayong, recognises individuals who have made significant contributions to the party’s struggle and grassroots work.

items.title: MOH to reopen four training institutes next year amid critical nurse shortage
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is strengthening three key strategies under the country’s health workforce reform to address the critical shortage of nurses, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said the three strategies involved increasing the number of nursing graduates, expanding career pathways and implementing direct recruitment and greater autonomy in staffing management. Dzulkefly said the move was important in meeting the country’s health workforce needs amid the increasingly complex challenges facing the health system.

items.title: Onn Hafiz: Bangsa Johor rental deposit aid of RM1,000 to roll out next year
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 15 — The Johor government is expected to introduce the RM1,000 Bangsa Johor rental deposit assistance next year to help people in the state who face difficulties coming up with the upfront payment for accommodation. They serve in Johor, are part of Bangsa Johor and are working for us,” he said. Onn Hafiz said the first phase of the rental deposit assistance would target about 10,000 recipients.

items.title: DoE detects seven hotspots in East Malaysia as transboundary haze worsens air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — A total of seven hotspots were detected in the country, with five in Sarawak and two in Sabah, as air quality deteriorates in several areas of Sarawak, which are currently recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels. “Moderate to dense localised smoke plumes were also observed, originating from hotspots in large parts of Kalimantan, central Sarawak and central Sumatra,” she said in a statement today. She said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan as well as western and central Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings.

items.title: Sabah-based KDM cuts ties with GRS govt, says it’s time to win back grassroots
items.summary: KINARUT, Aug 15 — Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) today pulled its support for the Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS)-led state government, signalling a shift in the party’s political direction ahead of the next general election. KDM acting president Priscella Peter said the decision was made by the party’s supreme council during its annual meeting today, local media reported. Priscella said the party had been affected by what happened after the previous state election, prompting it to make its position known well before the next polls.

items.title: If you’re naughty, we will know it, mayor warns as Kota Kinabalu adds 1,600 CCTV cameras to catch vandals
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — A total of 1,600 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras will be installed across the city soon as City Hall (DBKK) moves to strengthen surveillance and protect public assets from vandalism. Sabin also said the Kota Kinabalu International Mayors’ Dialogue 2026 would bring together mayors, city leaders, policymakers, development partners and other stakeholders to exchange ideas and practical experiences on the challenges and opportunities facing cities. He said Australian participation would provide an opportunity to strengthen practical cooperation and relationships between Kota Kinabalu and Australian cities, and expressed hope that the Australian High Commission could help facilitate the attendance of Australian city leaders.

items.title: Threat ends as Sabah wildlife officers kill 14-foot croc near in Sipitang river near jetty to Labuan
items.summary: SIPITANG, August 15 — A 14-foot male crocodile was caught and shot dead by the Sabah Wildlife Department (JHL) on Thursday, bringing relief to residents who had been living in fear of the reptile at Kampung Tanjung Pagar. The crocodile was frequently spotted at the mouth of the river near Kg Tanjung Pagar before it was shot dead and handed over to a licensed crocodile hunter. However, residents have been warned to remain cautious as other crocodiles could still be in the area.

items.title: Finance Ministry to roll out RM1.2b in STR cash aid for 5.3 million recipients from today
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said Phase 3 payments of the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid will be disbursed in stages starting today to 5.3 million recipients, with an allocation of RM1.2 billion. Of these, 3.9 million are low- and middle-income households, and 1.4 million are single senior citizens. The ministry said, depending on the category they fall under, recipients can collect up to RM3,300 in total by August 2026, combining STR Phases 1 to 3 and the monthly SARA basic aid.

items.title: He saw the crash online and knew something was wrong: Father loses wife, son in Temerloh crash
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Aug 15 — A routine wait for his wife’s arrival turned into a frantic search for answers after Saifulnizam Sulaiman realised she had not responded to his messages or calls for hours. Saifulnizam, 39, was in Seremban for work while his wife, Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and their 12-year-old son, Muhammad Fattah Aisy Naufal Saifulnizam, were travelling from Jerantut to join him during the school holidays. His worst fears grew after he came across social media posts about a crash along Jalan Temerloh-Triang.

items.title: New ‘One Higher Education Act’, launched in January, to replace UUCA, Zambry confirms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — A more comprehensive national higher education legislative framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) has been outlined under the Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026-2035, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir. He said the effort was part of the agenda for establishing the One Higher Education Act, which was launched in January 2026. Zambry said the Higher Education Ministry was taking into account the need to reform the national higher education legislative framework by drafting a new, more comprehensive act to replace UUCA.

items.title: Helicopter catches fire during engine test at Subang airport, four escape but one hit by debris
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 15 — A Kamov Ka-32 helicopter caught fire during an engine test at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here today, with four people escaping and one person reportedly injured after being struck by debris outside the aircraft. “The fire occurred as the helicopter was about to take off for the purpose of engine testing after repairs,” Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said in a statement today. Five firefighters from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were deployed with a Fire Rescue Tender to the scene.

items.title: MoH: No significant rise in haze-related illnesses yet
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — Malaysia has not recorded a significant increase in haze-related illnesses so far, but the Ministry of Health (MOH) does not rule out a rise in cases if air quality worsens or the haze persists. The MOH said no increase had been recorded so far in the three types of haze-related illnesses, namely upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis, monitored through sentinel health facilities. In Sarawak, the MOH said monitoring at 12 sentinel health clinics recorded a decline in URTI cases, from 1,473 in Epidemiological Week (EW) 31, before the haze, to 1,347 in EW 32.

items.title: MACC detains seven in Tabung Haji RCI probe, including senior executives and shipping company CEO
items.summary: According to sources, the suspects, comprising a chief executive officer, a former director, a director and four former TH senior executives, were arrested separately between 3pm and 10.30pm last night at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya. “The first suspect, a shipping company CEO with a ‘Datuk’ title in his 60s, was arrested on suspicion of submitting documents with false details when making payments to TH. “The second suspect is a construction company director with a ‘Datuk’ title, also in his 60s.
